**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 3 (0770/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Time allowed: THREE HOURS.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae and tables produced by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Electronic calculators may be used. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The weekly wages, in thousands, of a group of 80 part time workers in a certain bakery is as shown in the frequency distribution below.

| Wages (in thousands) | 1 - 10 | 11-20 | 21-30 | 31-40 | 41-50 | 51-60 | 61-70 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of workers | 5 | 15 | 22 | 18 | 10 | 8 | 2 |
incertitudes: Question 2 : les salaires sont supposés entiers (en milliers), donc les limites de classes sont 0.5, 10.5, 20.5, ..., 70.5 et les milieux 5.5, 15.5, ..., 65.5 (même convention que les autres sujets de la série). Avec les limites 0, 10, ..., 70 (milieux 5, 15, ...), la moyenne vaudrait 30.625 et la médiane lue sur la courbe 29.09 ; l'écart type ne change pas.

Question 2 (b) : la courbe n'est pas imprimée, c'est l'élève qui la trace : le corrigé donne le tableau des fréquences cumulées, les points à placer et le tracé attendu, sans figure PNG. Les parties (c) et (d) sont des lectures graphiques : le corrigé les calcule par interpolation linéaire entre deux points de la courbe (une lecture de 29.5 à 30 pour la médiane et de 6 à 7 travailleurs pour (d) est acceptable).
Question 2 (a) : l'écart type est celui de la distribution (diviseur $n = 80$), comme il est d'usage pour des données groupées ; avec le diviseur $n - 1$ on obtiendrait 14.74.
Question 2 : les points imprimés par partie, (7, 2, 2, 2), totalisent 13 ; recopiés tels quels.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the wages.
(b) Draw a cumulative frequency curve for this distribution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The wages are whole numbers, so the **upper class boundaries** are $10.5, 20.5, \ldots, 70.5$. Each cumulative frequency is plotted against the upper boundary of its class.

| Upper boundary | 0.5 | 10.5 | 20.5 | 30.5 | 40.5 | 50.5 | 60.5 | 70.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 0 | 5 | 20 | 42 | 60 | 70 | 78 | 80 |

**Drawing.** Horizontal axis: wages in thousands, from 0 to 70 (for example 2 cm for 10 thousand); vertical axis: cumulative frequency, from 0 to 80 (for example 2 cm for 10 workers). Plot the eight points $(0.5, 0)$, $(10.5, 5)$, $(20.5, 20)$, $(30.5, 42)$, $(40.5, 60)$, $(50.5, 70)$, $(60.5, 78)$, $(70.5, 80)$ and join them with a smooth S-shaped curve (an ogive), steepest between $x = 20.5$ and $x = 30.5$ where the class frequency is largest (22), and flattening after 50.5. Label both axes and give the graph a title.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using the cumulative frequency curve, estimate

(c) the median wage,
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median corresponds to the cumulative frequency $\dfrac{n}{2} = \dfrac{80}{2} = 40$. On the curve, draw a horizontal line from 40 on the vertical axis to the curve, then a vertical line down to the horizontal axis.

The point lies between $(20.5, 20)$ and $(30.5, 42)$, where the curve is almost straight, so by linear interpolation

$$\text{Median} = 20.5 + \frac{40 - 20}{42 - 20} \times 10 = 20.5 + \frac{200}{22} = 20.5 + 9.0909 = 29.59$$

**Median wage $\approx 29.6$ thousand, that is about 29 600 per week** (a graph reading between 29.5 and 30 is acceptable).

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) the number of workers who earn more than 55000 per week.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A wage of 55000 corresponds to $x = 55$ (in thousands). On the curve, draw a vertical line from $x = 55$ up to the curve, then a horizontal line across to the cumulative frequency axis: this reads the number of workers earning **at most** 55000.

The point lies between $(50.5, 70)$ and $(60.5, 78)$, so by linear interpolation

$$CF(55) = 70 + \frac{55 - 50.5}{60.5 - 50.5} \times (78 - 70) = 70 + 0.45 \times 8 = 73.6$$

The number earning **more than** 55000 is the remainder of the 80 workers:

$$80 - 73.6 = 6.4$$

**About 6 workers earn more than 55000 per week.**
